Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations Advisory To Shipping No. A-42-2026 November 9, 2026 TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Increase in the Number of Booking Slots at the Panamax Locks and in the Maximum Allowable Draft at the Neopanamax Locks Supported by improving water conditions, favorable hydrological projections, and the effectiveness of the water-saving measures implemented at the locks, the Panama Canal Authority (ACP) announces an additional booking slot at the Panamax Locks and an increase in the maximum allowable draft at the Neopanamax Locks. Effective immediately, the daily capacity for vessels in the Super category will increase from eighteen (18) to nineteen (19) slots. The additional slot will be offered as follows: through Booking Period 3 (Auction) for booking dates from November 12 to November 17, 2026; through Booking Period 2 (Special Competition) for booking dates from November 18 to 23, 2026, and for booking dates beginning November 24, 2026, at the opening of the 2nd Period Competition on November 10, 2026. With this adjustment, the total daily capacity will increase to 34 transit slots across the Neopanamax and Panamax Locks, providing customers greater access and planning flexibility. Additionally, based on the current and projected level of Gatun Lake for the following weeks, effective immediately and until further notice, the maximum authorized draft for vessels transiting the Neopanamax locks will be 15.24 m (50.0 feet). Therefore, vessels without a reservation may experience extremely extensive delays. 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023

Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations
Advisory to Shipping No. A-40-2026
October 30, 2026 TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Updated NetZero Slot Eligibility Requirements for First-Time Transit Vessels and Modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) continues to support and encourage investments in low-carbon and energy-efficient vessels through an update to the NetZero Slot Program. Under this update, first-transit vessels may participate in the NetZero Slot competition once the ACP has issued the required preliminary admeasurement inspection. 1. Requirements for First-Time Transit Vessels to Participate To participate in the NetZero Slot competition, first-time vessels must obtain a preliminary admeasurement inspection from the Panama Canal Admeasurement Unit prior to the competition date. This preliminary determination must include the following information needed to evaluate the vessel for the competition date: • Toll basis • Panama Canal Universal Measurement System (PC/UMS) tonnage • Review of all pertinent information for the vessel database, including the engine type and the vessel’s eligibility for the NetZero Program • Any other vessel information required by the ACP. 2. How Customers May Request a Preliminary Admeasurement Inspection Vessel owners, operators, or authorized vessel agents interested in participating in the NetZero Slot competition with first-time vessels may request a preliminary admeasurement determination through the Panama Canal Admeasurement Unit, in accordance with ACP-established procedures. Requests shall include the technical documentation and information required by the ACP and are subject to applicable fees and charges. Submission of a request does not, itself, establish eligibility. Eligibility will be confirmed only after the Panama Canal Admeasurement Unit has completed the required evaluation and issued the corresponding preliminary admeasurement inspection. 3. Admeasurement Review and Vessel Inspection The ACP may issue the preliminary admeasurement determination supported by the documents submitted and, when necessary, a vessel inspection. A vessel inspection may be conducted outside the Republic of Panama under Maritime Service Tariff Item 1080, Vessel Inspections Overseas, Subject to Customer Request. The applicable tariff will depend on the inspection location, as shown below:
3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023
OP, October 30, 2026 Subject: Updated NetZero Slot Eligibility Requirements for First-Time Transit Vessels and Modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System
Customer shall be responsible for all applicable fees, charges, and expenses associated with the overseas vessel inspection service and the corresponding admeasurement inspection, including travel-related expenses not included in the published tariff.
The customer shall also be responsible for making all necessary arrangements for the proper inspection of the vessel at the corresponding port, including obtaining the required permits and ensuring appropriate access to the vessel.
For further information on these tariffs, please refer to the following links: https://pancanal.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Maritime-tariffs-80-cancellation-feb26.pdf https://pancanal.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Notes-on-tolls-and-maritime-tariffs-febrero- 202675.pdf
4. Important Reminder A first-time transit vessel that receives the required preliminary admeasurement inspection may participate in the NetZero Slot competition, provided that the vessel also complies with all other eligibility requirements and procedures established for the NetZero Program. The preliminary admeasurement inspection will be used to establish the vessel information required for participation in the competition. It does not replace the final verification or any inspection that the ACP may require upon the vessel’s arrival in Canal waters or prior to transit. Customers must submit the required information well in advance of their intended competition date to provide the Panama Canal Authority (ACP) sufficient time to complete the applicable procedures, including the Preliminary Admeasurement Inspection outside the Republic of Panama. Timely submission is essential to ensure that all requirements are completed prior to the competition date, thereby maintaining the customer’s eligibility to participate in the NetZero competition. Customers who have not completed the required process by the applicable competition date will be ineligible to participate in the NetZero competition. Modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) announces modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System, including the reversal of a temporary measure introduced in July 2026 in response to changes in global shipping patterns that placed additional pressure on transit demand. As vessel traffic has since normalized, the ACP will return to the previous allocation criteria. Therefore, effective immediately, during Booking Periods 1A and 2 for the Neopanamax locks, any slot that is cancelled or otherwise becomes available will be allocated through a Special Competition using the following order of priority: Full Container, LNG, LPG, and Car Carrier/RoRo vessels. Within each vessel category, the first tiebreaker will be TTA, when applicable, followed by customer ranking as the second tiebreaker. While the water deficit in the Canal watershed persists, the Transit Reservation (Booking) System remains the only mechanism to guarantee a transit date. Therefore, vessels without a reservation may experience extremely extensive delays. The Canal remains committed to closely monitoring water conditions and rainfall levels and will communicate any further adjustments in a timely manner, as circumstances warrant. For any further inquiries regarding these rules, please contact: operationservices@pancanal.com
ORIGINAL SIGNED Boris Moreno Vásquez Vice President for Operations

Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations Advisory To Shipping No. A-39-2026 October 21, 2026 TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System Considering the effectiveness of the water saving measures implemented at the Locks and the positive impact of recent close to average precipitation levels on the Canal watershed, the Panama Canal Authority (ACP) has been able to sustain the number of transits being offered at the Panamax Locks, therefore, effective immediately, we are pleased to announce the reinstalment of the Last-Minute Reservation service at the Panamax Locks. The Last-Minute Reservation service will be made available in accordance with the criteria and rules set forth in Notice to Shipping N-07 when a slot becomes available and the ACP, at its sole discretion, decides to offer such slot. Additionally, the rules mentioned in the Notice to Shipping N-07, article 23, section 12, regarding the rules for Swaps and Substitutions between Alliance Members that were only available for Neopanamax vessels, will also be available for vessels in the Super category for booking dates beginning January 3, 2027. Please note that all other Swap and Substitution rules set forth in the N-07 remain in effect. While the water deficit in the Canal watershed persists, the Transit Reservation (Booking) System remains the only mechanism to guarantee a transit date. Therefore, vessels without a reservation may experience extremely extensive delays. The Canal remains committed to closely monitoring water conditions and rainfall levels and will communicate any further adjustments in a timely manner, as circumstances warrant. For inquiries regarding these measures, please contact: operationservices@pancanal.com ORIGINAL SIGNED Boris Moreno Vásquez Vice President for Operations 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023

Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations Advisory To Shipping No. A-37-2026 October 5, 2026 TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Long-Term Slot Allocation Program 2027 and Modification to Transit Reservation System tariffs To facilitate customer planning for the 2027 dry season, the Panama Canal Authority (ACP) will offer Long- Term Slot Allocation (LoTSA) programs for transit dates from January 3 through April 3, 2027. LoTSA Neopanamax will continue under its current terms, while the new LoTSA Panamax Pilot Program will extend advance slot allocation to customers transiting the Panamax Locks. What the program is designed to do LoTSA allows customers to secure a package of transit slots for the full period in a single transaction, reducing their reliance on daily booking competitions. By committing part of the Canal’s projected transit capacity earlier, the program enhances planning certainty, particularly when water availability is limited. Neopanamax: continuity for customers with recurring itineraries LoTSA Neopanamax will continue under the current award mechanism, selection criteria, and tie-breaking rules, with an average of three (3) slots per day. Customers may therefore secure transits for the full period under familiar terms. Panamax: a new planning option for segments that did not have one For the first time, customers transiting the Panamax locks may secure slots in advance through a sealed-bid auction. The pilot will use the same award mechanism, selection criteria, and tie-breaking rules as LoTSA Neopanamax and will offer an average of three (3) slots per day. It is intended for fixed-itinerary customers and those whose customer-ranking position makes it more difficult to obtain slots through the regular booking system. How are the slots offered? • Only Fixed packages will be offered, with a single level of flexibility and characteristics tailored to the operational needs of eligible segments. • Slots will be distributed according to package type and transit direction, for each set of locks. • A new FixSlot package is introduced for all other market segments, excluding Full Container, LNG, and LPG vessels. Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations
Advisory to Shipping No. A-35-2026
September 16, 2026. TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Clarification on Consecutive Booking Dates Limitation in the Panamax Locks Across Different Booking Periods
The Panama Canal Authority hereby clarifies the application of the booking eligibility rules related to consecutive booking dates in the Transit Reservation System for the Panamax Locks. This clarification is provided in connection with the provisions introduced through Advisory to Shipping No. A-28-2026 regarding booking slot eligibility across competitions and special competitions conducted in different booking periods. All other Panamax booking slot allocation rules published in Advisory to Shipping No. A- 28-2026 remain in effect and are not affected by this clarification.
Effective immediately, the restriction on obtaining booking slots for consecutive transit dates shall not apply when the bookings are awarded through different booking periods. This clarification applies exclusively to Panamax Locks.
Accordingly, a customer that has been awarded a booking slot for a transit date during Booking Period 1 may also participate in, and be awarded, a booking slot for the following transit date during Booking Period 2, subject to slot availability and compliance with all other applicable reservation process requirements.
This clarification is intended to ensure a consistent interpretation of the current rules, avoid unintended restrictions and provide customers with greater clarity and predictability when planning multiple transits.
Consequently, the consecutive booking date limitation shall apply only within the same booking period and shall not prevent customers from obtaining booking slots for consecutive transit dates when such slots are awarded through different booking periods.
For any further inquiries regarding these rules, please contact: operationservices@pancanal.com.
ORIGINAL SIGNED Boris Moreno Vásquez Vice President for Operations 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023

Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations
Advisory To Shipping No. A-32-2026
September 2, 2026 TO:
All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Postponement of the Late Cancellation Surcharge Fee (Tariff No. 1050.IBC9)
The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) continues to closely monitor operational conditions and customer needs while implementing measures to preserve transit reliability and optimize the use of available capacity.
As previously announced in Advisory to Shipping No. A-28-2026, the ACP planned to implement the Late Cancellation Surcharge Fee (Tariff No. 1050.IBC9) effective September 1, 2026. However, after further evaluating current conditions and providing customers with additional time to adapt to this measure, the ACP has decided to postpone its implementation until further notice.
Accordingly, the Late Cancellation Surcharge Fee (Tariff No. 1050.IBC9) will not be applied on September 1, 2026, as previously announced.
The ACP will communicate a new implementation date through a future Advisory to Shipping, providing sufficient advance notice to all customers.
The Canal remains committed to maintaining transparent communication with its customers and will continue to monitor operational and market conditions to ensure the efficient and equitable allocation of transit capacity.
For inquiries regarding these measures, please contact: operationservices@pancanal.com
ORIGINAL SIGNED Boris Moreno Vásquez Vice President for Operations 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023

Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations Advisory to Shipping No. A-31-2026 August 28, 2026 TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Transit Reservation (Booking) System - Rule modifications The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) is introducing temporary modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System. These adjustments have been developed after carefully considering customer feedback and suggestions and reflect the ACP’s ongoing commitment to providing the highest level of service possible, ensuring the efficient management of Canal operations, and supporting the sustainable use of water resources. The changes are intended to allocate booking slots as equitably as possible across market segments while prioritizing vessels that make more efficient use of water. The following measures will take effect on the dates indicated below. Neopanamax Locks Slot Allocation Effective August 30, 2026, for booking dates beginning September 13, 2026: 1. Customers will be allowed to obtained more than one slot per booking date, therefore, the following rule published in the Advisory A28-2026 will not apply to Neopanamax vessels “Customers that have already been awarded booking slots in previous periods, including Long Term Slot Allocation (LoTSA) and Net Zero for the same booking date, will not be allowed to obtain a slot during current competition, unless there are no additional competitors.” 2. Customers will be allowed to obtain booking slots for two or more consecutive booking dates, therefore, the following rule published in the Advisory A28-2026 will not apply to Neopanamax vessels “Customers that have already been awarded booking slots for the previous booking date, including LoTSA and Net Zero, will not be allowed to obtain a slot during the following booking date competition, unless there are no additional competitors.” 3. Sixty-three (63) Slots will be offered per week. 4. The following table shows the slot distribution including the slots allocated through LoTSA and NetZero and compliments the slot distribution table per booking period published in the Advisory A29- 2026.

Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations
Advisory to Shipping No. A-30-2026
August 25, 2026
TO : All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT : Modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System
The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) announces modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System to provide greater clarity regarding existing rules and requirements. These revisions will prevent misunderstandings and unintended interpretations that could affect the transparency, consistency, and overall effectiveness of the booking process. Therefore, effective immediately, the following changes will be implemented: The paragraph in the Article 22, section “6. Advisory to Shipping No. A-29-2026
August 20, 2026 TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Additional Measures to Address Reduced Precipitation in the Canal Watershed
Despite the arrival of the rainy season in the Isthmus of Panama and the water-saving measures implemented by the Panama Canal Authority (ACP) in recent months to mitigate the adverse effects of the El Niño event, current watershed conditions continue to warrant additional preventive measures to support the long-term sustainability of Canal operations. During the current hydrological year (May through August), cumulative rainfall across the Canal watershed has been 34% below the historical average, while watershed inflows have been 44% below their historical average for the same period, reflecting a substantially reduced hydrologic response despite the onset of the rainy season. Furthermore, forecasts indicate that the anticipated severity of the 2026-2027 El Niño event could further reduce precipitation and runoff during the remainder of the wet season. The combination of these observed deficits and the forecast of a potentially severe 2026-2027 El Niño event raises concerns regarding water availability during the upcoming 2027 dry season (January to April). These conditions require vigilant monitoring and prudent water resource management to always ensure the reliable and sustainable operation of the Canal. Particularly during the 2023-2024 El Niño event, the Canal maintained full open and timely communications with agents, owners and operators on the existing hydrological conditions of the waterway, a practice that we maintain at all times regardless of its criticality, as these hydrological conditions, is an essential aspect of our mutual interest. The measures described below are therefore being implemented to preserve service reliability, safeguard water resources for human consumption, and provide customers with timely and transparent information to support voyage planning and supply chain decisions. Effective August 21, 2026, for booking dates beginning September 4, 2026, the number of daily slots available at the Neopanamax Locks will be adjusted to nine (9). Accordingly, only one (1) slot will be offered during Booking Period 2. Additionally, the number of daily slots available at the Panamax Locks will be adjusted to twenty-five (25). Accordingly, only one (1) slot will be offered to Regular vessels during Booking Period 2. Due to the reduction in available transit slots during Booking Period 2, Conditioned slot in the Neopanamax category will not be available.

TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Transit Reservation (Booking) System - Rule modifications The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) continues to experience climatic disruptions due to the current El Niño event, which is causing below-average rainfall and reduced water inflows to its reservoirs. To help ensure reliable Canal operations and preserve the draft available to customers, the ACP is introducing temporary modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System. These changes are intended to allocate slots in the most equitable manner as possible, across market segments and prioritize vessels that make more efficient use of water. The following measures will take effect on the dates indicated below. Auctions methodology Given the current climate conditions and to promote a more equitable allocation process, considering market composition, including cargo type, market segment characteristics, and vessel operating models, the ACP will temporarily make selected auction slots available by market segment group. Similarly to what was temporarily implemented on November 29, 2023, this method aims to provide additional opportunities for different market segment vessels. Effective August 21, 2026, for booking dates beginning September 4, 2026, auction slots designated for Neopanamax, Super and Regular vessels may be made available to vessels within specific market segments, organized into groups, as shown in the following table: Group 1 Group 2 Group 3 Group 4 • Liquified Natural Gas • Liquified Petroleum Gas • Dry Bulk • General Cargo • Others • Full Container • Vehicle Carriers / RoRo • Refrigerated • Chemical Tankers • Crude/Product Tankers
The ACP will announce the day of the week on which the auction slot will be made available to each group. The specific dates on which the groups (one or more) identified above may participate in the auctions will be determined based on the number of vessels awaiting transit within each group and will be communicated through the Projected Booking Slots Availability table, published daily. Slot allocation Similarly to what was temporarily implemented on December 15, 2023, this method aims to provide additional opportunities for different customers, only one booking slot will be allowed per customer per day during the competition as shown in the following table:

Customers that have already been awarded booking slots for the previous booking date, including LoTSA and Net Zero, will not be allowed to obtain a slot during the following booking date competition, unless there are no additional competitors. 3. The limit per customer does not apply to slots awarded through the auction process. 4. In the Neopanamax Locks, full container vessels with maximum TEU capacity will have priority to obtain a slot during competition. For vessels with the same TEU capacity, the Customer Ranking will be used as the tiebreaker criteria. Once a slot is assigned, customers will be allowed to swap or substitute the vessel with another vessel of the same or greater TEU capacity. Any customer preference submitted during the reservation slot allocation process will also be limited to vessels with the same or greater TEU capacity. 5. Unused slots from the Special Period for Super and Regular vessels for booking dates beginning November 20, 2026, will be carried over to Period 2. 6. Unused slots from the Special Period have already transferred to Period 1 for Super and Regular vessels for booking dates beginning September 5, 2026, to November 19, 2026, will be carried over to Period 2. 7. The transit conditions changes table published in Notice to Shipping N-07 will not apply until further notice.
Other announcements To manage the current situation, additional modifications will be implemented and effective immediately: 1. The availability of flexibility services (such as change date, transit in advance, substitutions, etc.) may be narrowed down for all customers. For LoTSA program customers, deferrals and advanced services may be also limited under the current circumstances. 2. The Last-Minute service will be suspended until further notice. Furthermore, forfeited vessels must obtain a new slot to reschedule their transit.
Measures applicable in September 1. Effective September 1, 2026, the Canal will apply the late cancellation surcharge fee (tariff number 1050.IBC9) in addition to the applicable cancellation fee, when a booking is cancelled 7 days or less before
